notes.shape: A table row per vendor number, each with a status cell that names the owner as a category ('Anthropic-prescribed') and nothing else. The facts sit in the middle column and the attribution sits in the last, in a form that reads as provenance.
notes.carve_outs: None apply. The status cell is not a conforming record: it names no page, no as-of date and no recheck trigger. The file is not a distillation of the named source; it is a grading aid that carries the numbers incidentally.
notes.rubric: R1 holds: the product's own documentation owns the listing cap and the budget. R2 holds: a character count and a percentage. R3 holds: each row states the number as the current bound. R4 holds: a status tag names an owner and supplies none of the record's other three parts, so the fact is stated without a whole four-part record.
notes.carries: This is the case that tests whether an owner named in a category cell is mistaken for attribution. A run that clears it on the word 'Anthropic-prescribed' has treated a label as a record.
notes.tier_reason: A source was supplied, so source-fetched-similar, and never fingerprint-confirmed for this class. Report-only.
